newsitem.title: USA: Union to continue UPS talks past midnight deadline.
newsitem.headline: Union to continue UPS talks past midnight deadline.

text.p: The Teamster Union said Thursday it would keep talking to United Parcel Service past a midnight strike deadline, postponing its walkout.
"The word is they will keep negotiating," a spokeswoman for the union said. She said that meant union members would not walk off their jobs after the deadline to agree a new contract elapsed.

Just past midnight, there was no sign that talks had ended at the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service headquarters, where union and company officials were meeting to avert a strike that could cripple UPS, the nation's largest parcel carrier.

Teamsters spokesman Rand Wilson told reporters just before midnight he had been told by union negotiators that contract talks were continuing and that union members should wait for further instructions.
"Our members are waiting for instructions from the national negotiating committee," Wilson said.
